simple.meaning: רֵיקָם (rêyqâm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “emptily ; figuratively (objective) ineffectually , (subjective) undeservedly.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 16 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Ruth, 1 Samuel, and 5 more, beginning at Genesis 31:42. Its contexts include birth, family, family line, firstborn, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֵיקָם (H7387).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רֵיקָם (rêyqâm) / H7387 is traced through Genesis 31:42, Exodus 3:21, Exodus 23:15, Exodus 34:20 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: without cause, empty, in vain, void.
definitions.full: H7387. reqam רֵיקָם adverb emptily, vainly ; — 1 in empty condition, empty = with empty hands; with verb of sending Gen 31:42 (E), Deut 15:13 ; 1Sam 6:3 ; Job 22:9 ; of going forth Exod 3:21 , returning Ruth 1:21 ; 3:17 ; = without an offering, ד פָנַי יֵרָאוּ ׳לֹא Exod 23:15 (E) = 34:20 (J), more fully Deut 16:16 (compare [ פָנֶה ] II. 2 ראה Niph`al 1 b ). 2 in vain, without effect : with שׁוּב 2Sam 1:22 (poem), Isa 55:11 ; Jer 14:3 (but see רֵיק 1 ), Jer 50:9 ; probably also ר ׳צוֺרֲרִי Psa 7:5 those who were my adversaries in vain (without success); ר ׳הַבּוֺגְדִים 25:3 that deal treacherously in vain <in both most without cause ).

occurrences.englishText: Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”
I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and it will happen that when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.

You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it you came out of Egypt), and no one shall appear before me empty.
You shall redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb. If you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck. You shall redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before me empty.
When you let him go free from you, you shall not let him go empty.

Three times in a year all of your males shall appear before Yahweh your God in the place which he chooses: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of booths. They shall not appear before Yahweh empty.
I went out full, and Yahweh has brought me home again empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since Yahweh has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?”
She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley; for he said, ‘Don’t go empty to your mother-in-law.’ ”

They said, “If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, don’t send it empty; but by all means return a trespass offering to him. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.”
